text.p: Danish cleaning group ISS said on Friday that Executive Vice-President Joern Wendel Andersen had offered his resignation over unspecified differences with fellow-directors.
"Disagreement has arisen between Joern Wendel Andersen and other directors in areas of particular strategic importance," Chairman Arne Madsen said in a statement.
The board was considering Andersen's decision and both sides had agreed to make no further comment, the statement said.
Andersen, who is also Chief Financial Officer, is number two in the group after CEO Waldemar Schmidt.
The company had a stormy time in 1996, when falsified accounts in its U.S. unit ISS Inc. led to a first-half 1996 group loss of 2.0 billion crowns.

Then came fines against directors Sven Ipsen and Poul Andreassen, the firm's founder and former chief, for telling industry colleagues about the crisis before the Copenhagen Stock Exchange was informed. Andreassen later left the board.

But last December's sale of ISS.Inc boosted ISS' credit rating and restored its share, now trading at a healthy 185 crowns compared to a low of 95 crowns when news of the U.S. disaster was announced and up from 163 crowns before the fall.
